title: Add scheduler saturation metrics (queue depth, backpressure, admission control) to metrics pipeline
author: Nadia Rahman
body:
## Summary
Adds a small set of standardized scheduler saturation metrics to the Redwood metrics pipeline so we can reliably diagnose (and alert on) scheduler contention vs. downstream GPU/runtime issues. This is intended to support Incident Bot v2 context cards and reduce “is it capacity vs config vs deploy?” time in the first 5 minutes.

## Motivation
During recent Sev1/Sep2 incidents we had GPU utilization and request error rates, but not enough visibility into the scheduler layer itself. In particular:
- We couldn’t distinguish GPU saturation from scheduler queueing (high queue depth / high queue wait) when batching settings changed.
- We lacked a consistent backpressure indicator when admission control kicked in.
- Existing per-component gauges were inconsistent across hosted and dedicated pools and weren’t being exported with stable label sets.

## What’s in this PR
### New metrics (exported)
All metrics are emitted from the scheduler and exported via the existing OTel -> metrics pipeline.
- `redwood.scheduler.queue.depth` (gauge): current queue depth at scheduler admission.
- `redwood.scheduler.queue.wait_ms` (histogram): time spent waiting in scheduler queue prior to admission.
- `redwood.scheduler.backpressure.active` (gauge, 0/1): whether backpressure is currently asserted for a pool.
- `redwood.scheduler.backpressure.drop_total` (counter): requests dropped/failed fast due to backpressure.
- `redwood.scheduler.admission.reject_total` (counter): admission control rejects (e.g., pool overloaded / max inflight).
- `redwood.scheduler.inflight` (gauge): currently admitted inflight requests tracked by scheduler.
- `redwood.scheduler.admission.limit` (gauge): configured inflight limit (exported for context; useful when config changes).

### Labels / cardinality guardrails
To keep series count bounded and bot queries cheap:
- Allowed labels: `region`, `pool`, `service`, `route`, `deployment_mode` (hosted|dedicated|private)
- Explicitly NOT labeled by tenant/customer/model_version/request_id.
- `route` is normalized (existing route-normalizer) and capped (unknown -> `other`).

### Pipeline changes
- Extends `metrics/registry/scheduler_metrics.ts` and wiring in scheduler runtime.
- Adds `metrics/allowlist.yaml` entries for the above names.
- Adds exporter mapping for histogram buckets and renames to match existing naming conventions.

### Tests
- Unit tests for metric emission paths (queue depth gauge and admission reject counters).
- Golden snapshot test for allowlist + exporter mapping.
- Integration test verifies metrics appear in the local metrics sink with expected label set (region/pool/service only).

## Rollout / risk
- Metrics are additive.
- Backpressure gauges/counters are behind an internal runtime flag `scheduler.metrics.backpressure_export` default ON in staging, ON in prod after 24h.
- Histogram volume: `queue.wait_ms` is sampled at 1.0% by default; can be increased temporarily for incident analysis.

## Follow-ups (not included)
- Add/update dashboards and alert thresholds in observability-pack (separate PR).
- Wire these signals into Incident Bot v2 saturation card (ENG-5423 follow-up tasks in incident-bot repo).

## Validation
- Staging: verified new series present for `us-east-1` hosted pool; queue wait histogram populated under synthetic load.
- Prod canary: verified no increase in metrics pipeline ingestion errors; series count increase within budget (+~1.8k time series across all regions/pools).

Refs: ENG-5423, incident-bot diagnostics initiative; aligns with ongoing saturation signal standardization work.
commits: e7b3b2c metrics: add scheduler saturation metric definitions and registry wiring
2c5e9f1 scheduler: emit queue depth/inflight gauges and admission reject counters
a91d0d7 metrics-pipeline: update allowlist and exporter mapping for scheduler metrics
7f42b30 tests: add golden snapshot for allowlist/exporter + integration smoke test
d0a6c19 chore: normalize route label and cap unknown routes to reduce cardinality
conversation:
Logan Wright (review): Can we confirm we are not emitting tenant_id anywhere on these? Also concerned about `route` label explosion if it includes full paths.

Nadia Rahman (author): Confirmed: scheduler emission points only pass region/pool/service/route/deployment_mode. No tenant context available in scheduler layer. For `route`, this uses the same normalizer as gateway metrics (template routes), plus a cap so anything unmapped goes to `other`. Added an integration test asserting label keys.

Allison Grant (review): Naming: we’ve been using dot-separated names in OTel, but dashboards/alerts often use Prom-style. Are we consistent with the rest of the pipeline?

Nadia Rahman: Yep—OTel names are dot-separated (`redwood.scheduler.queue.depth`) and exporter mapping keeps existing conventions. The dashboard PR will reference the exported names via the standard macro.

Aisha Bello (review): Histogram sampling at 1% is good, but incident-bot may want p95 queue wait. With sampling, do we lose utility?

Nadia Rahman: For bot context we plan to use gauge/counter signals for “is it queueing/backpressure?” and link to dashboards for deeper percentiles. We can temporarily bump sampling via runtime flag if needed. Added note in PR + flag description.

Ravi Menon (review): Admission limit gauge—where does it come from? Config propagation can be partial during incidents; please ensure it’s pulled from the scheduler’s active config, not control-plane desired state.

Nadia Rahman: Good call. Updated to export the scheduler’s effective runtime config (post-merge + defaults). Added a comment and a test to ensure we’re reading from `SchedulerConfig::effective()`.

Jacob Stein (review): Please add a short section in the metric docs about interpretation: queue depth high + gpu util low means scheduler contention vs GPU saturation.

Nadia Rahman: Added inline docstrings and a brief blurb in `scheduler_metrics.ts` for interpretation; runbook/docs update will be in follow-up (ENG-5431).

Final: reviewers approved after label normalization + effective config export changes.
release_notes: Internal only: Scheduler now exports saturation metrics (queue depth, queue wait, backpressure, admission rejects) with bounded label sets to improve incident diagnostics and power Incident Bot v2 context.
